UT-2026-SB312.policyArea: Education, K-12 Education, Local Education Agencies (LEAs)
UT-2026-SB312.aiSummary: The law changes rules for teacher licenses and discipline in Utah. It adds a new system for when a person with a suspended or revoked license can be kept from working or volunteering in a public school, with stricter limits for serious harm or sexual misconduct and fewer limits for technical mistakes. It also changes notice and hearing steps for license denials and other discipline, and it was signed by the governor.

UT-2026-SB252.policyArea: Administrative Rulemaking, Administrative Rulemaking and Procedures, Department of Government Operations
UT-2026-SB252.aiSummary: The bill sets water-use rules for state-owned buildings and grounds. It limits lawn and turf at many new or rebuilt state facilities, requires state agencies to cut outdoor water use, and asks them to use low-water plants and better irrigation methods. It also requires regular audits of irrigation systems and makes the Division of Facilities Construction and Management check and report on water efficiency. The law takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HB158.aiSummary: The bill would rename the offense and expand it to cover using a tracking device on a person or certain personal property, or using a tracking app to follow someone’s movements. It also says the offense can still apply if someone kept using the tracker after consent was taken back. In civil cases, a person hurt by this conduct could seek damages, including a set amount of $50 a day or $5,000, whichever is greater, and the bill takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HB137.aiSummary: The bill creates a state grant fund to help law enforcement agencies solve violent crimes. The State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice would run the fund and give grants to agencies to help raise violent crime clearance rates, which means cases cleared by arrest or by other set means. UT-2026-HB122.policyArea: Correctional Facilities, Department of Corrections, Health Care
UT-2026-HB122.aiSummary: The bill would add rules for pregnant and postpartum inmates in Utah jails and prisons. It would require reporting on pregnant inmates and inmates who are parents of minor children, set postpartum recovery at 12 weeks after birth, and require 12 weeks of access to social worker help and postpartum care. It also would limit when restraints can be used during postpartum recovery and let health care providers make certain decisions about pregnant inmates.

UT-2026-HB389.aiSummary: The bill changes Utah rules for cannabis, hemp, and medical cannabis. It would require industrial hemp retailers to check ID to confirm a buyer is at least 21, remove some video camera rules for those retailers, and let medical cannabis processors make some low-THC products and pharmacies sell them. It also moves medical cannabis program duties and a patient fund to the Department of Agriculture and Food, changes a board name and makeup, and adds a fee on medical cannabis purchases to help pay for enforcement. The governor signed it.

UT-2026-HB185.policyArea: Administrative Rulemaking and Procedures, Air Quality, Attorney General
UT-2026-HB185.aiSummary: This bill would set new rules for the sale or exchange of carbon credits by state entities. It would create a Carbon Credit Litigation Fund, require those state entities to report on carbon credit sales, and require the state auditor to report on those sales to a legislative budget subcommittee. It would also make changes to related state audit and air quality laws.
